the ATLAS data for prompt J/ψ + Z boson production at s=8 TeV are not incompatible with the CEM and that, if one assumes that the ATLAS extraction of the SPS contribution is correct, the CEM nonperturbative parameter is reduced from its LO value by about 20% at NLO.
the NLO SPS cross section is smaller than the NLO NRQSD prediction and is in good agreement with the ATLAS data after taking the DPS contribution and the ATLAS systematic uncertainties into account.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have performed an NLO computation of a process for which no NLO evaluation exists, and we have also performed the first N LO computation of dσ / dPT for prompt single J/ψ production.
the CEM is a viable model to describe prompt single-J/psi production at NLO.
the NLO SPS yield is smaller than the ATLAS SPS yield by a factor as small as 1.3 and that the NLO yield is smaller than that of the LO yield by a factor 0.7.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SPS cross sections for prompt single-Jψ and J/ψZ production are likely to be significantly smaller than the current theoretical estimates.
the CEM NLO fit is in good agreement with the ATLAS data, which provides a strong argument in favor of this model.
the NLO SPS cross section in the CEM is about 2.5 times smaller than the NLO SBS cross section, which is the main reason of the discrepancy with the ATLAS data.
